title: ISSM: change upstream shelf thickness
chapter_timing: Receipt-bound logical chapters include control cue, actual transition and confirmation; durations are video times.

steps.title: Your goal: change the shelf thickness profile
instructions: Run an owned SquareIceShelf clone with hmax = 1010 m while keeping hmin = 300 m.
Prepare Square.par with only hmax changed from 1000 to 1010 m.
Open CryoLauncher and sign in. Use an approved connected cloud account with its resources prepared.
The following steps select this tutorial’s model and example.
steps.why: Keep the source inputs, inspect native fields, and save a complete result package. Your workspace keeps scripts, dataset references and results together.
steps.expected: Your workspace keeps scripts, datasets, run history and results together.
steps.note: Use an already connected cloud account, configured MATLAB license and any required Connector. Shared application orientation; the case-specific configuration follows.

steps.title: 1. Choose the native Advanced case
instructions: Choose Cloud → Advanced → ISSM → SquareIceShelf.
Keep the application source intact and work in an owned clone.
steps.why: Choose the intended interface, model and example before editing or launching a run.
steps.expected: Retain your configured MATLAB license and required Connector.
steps.note: The native run uses diagnostic SSA stress balance.

steps.title: 2. Clone to your workspace
instructions: Enter a new example name and choose Clone to My Workspace.
Wait for the cloned-workspace confirmation.
The new example is pilot-issm-advanced-1119 and keeps the native example files.
steps.why: Cloning gives you an editable copy while preserving the supplied application source.
steps.expected: Keep the native example files in your owned clone.
steps.note: The canonical example remains read-only. You can now replace the parameter file in your own copy.

steps.title: 3. Select the changed parameter file
instructions: Choose script files. In your file picker select Square.par and choose Open.
The picker changes from zero to one selected script file.
You are replacing Square.par in the owned clone.
steps.why: Selecting local files prepares them for import; importing saves them in this example.
steps.expected: You are replacing Square.par in the owned clone.
steps.note: Your copy changes only hmax to 1010 m. Keep runme.m, DomainOutline.exp and Front.exp unchanged.

steps.title: 4. Enable intentional replacement
instructions: Enable Replace existing script files.
The clone already contains Square.par, so the replacement must be explicit.
Choose Import script files.
Wait for Imported Square.par. Files are saved.
The submitted file was checked against the intended hmax = 1010 m copy.
steps.why: Replacement explicitly allows an imported file to overwrite the same name in this clone. Import saves the selected source files in this example; it does not launch the model.
steps.expected: The submitted parameter file was checked against the intended copy.
steps.note: Check the selected filename before importing. The replacement checkbox is enabled for this existing file. The import replaces the file; an inline edit is not needed.

steps.title: 5. Keep the native run target
instructions: Keep runme.m as the Run target. It requests two MPI processes.
hmin stays 300 m. The +10 m change at hmax tapers along the y-dependent thickness profile.
steps.why: Run target selects the entry script; other imported files can act as helpers.
steps.expected: The +10 m change at hmax tapers along y; it is not a uniform addition.
steps.note: The thickness addition is not uniform over the shelf.

steps.title: 6. Review the native run
instructions: Choose Review & Launch and check ISSM, the owned example and runme.m.
Confirm Model: ISSM and Example: pilot-issm-advanced-1119.
Check the readiness results before submitting.
Choose Launch cloud run when the readiness checks are ready.
This confirmation starts the run.
Wait for the new ISSM Advanced card to replace the previous run card. Confirm pilot-issm-advanced-1119 before following its status.
Wait for completion, then open its results.
steps.why: Review confirms the intended model, source, resources and charges before submission. This confirmation stages the reviewed inputs and starts a paid cloud job. The previous card remains visible while the new run is registered.
steps.note: Retain the existing licensed MATLAB workflow. The native job used 2 vCPU and 8 GiB. Control guide; the following card belongs to this tutorial’s original native run. Setup and editing time are separate from model runtime.

steps.title: 7. Render the stress-balance result
instructions: The first field is previewed automatically. Select StressbalanceSolution → Vel and use Render when needed.
Vx, Vy, Vel and Pressure are finite at all 91 nodes.
The native mesh has 91 vertices and 148 triangles.
steps.why: The solution, field name, units and mesh counts identify what you are viewing.
steps.expected: Vx, Vy, Vel and Pressure are finite at all 91 nodes; 148 triangles.
steps.note: Read the field units and use the saved full figure for detail. Result identity comes from this run’s archive, rather than the launch-form selector.

steps.title: 8. Inspect the full velocity map
instructions: Open the unchanged saved velocity PNG.
Speed spans 0–9272.778005 m/year. The x and y axes are metres.
steps.why: The unchanged saved figure preserves the complete map, axes and colour scale.
steps.expected: Speed: 0–9272.778005 m/year; x and y are metres.
steps.note: The saved Vel agrees with hypot(Vx, Vy).

steps.title: 9. Read convergence correctly
instructions: StressbalanceConvergenceNumSteps is a scalar value of 23.
It reports diagnostic stress-balance convergence, not a transient time axis.
steps.why: A steady diagnostic convergence count is different from a transient time axis.
steps.expected: 23 steps is a scalar stress-balance convergence count.
steps.note: The other four exported fields are 91-node arrays.

steps.title: 10. Separate readiness and measured runtime
instructions: The native job succeeded with exit code 0.
Submission → Batch start: 183.642 s. Batch task: 36.831 s.
steps.why: Submission, queue/startup and native model execution are separate stages.
steps.expected: Submission → start: 183.642 s; Batch task: 36.831 s.
steps.note: Runtime provenance records MATLAB R2024b Update 7 and ISSM 2026.1.

steps.title: 11. Save this run’s archive
instructions: Choose Download results, then open the fresh HTTPS link.
Save the 11-member ZIP: numeric fields, mesh, native PNG, final MATLAB model and runtime/RNG provenance.
steps.why: The archive keeps this run’s numeric outputs, figures and provenance together.
steps.expected: Keep it with your modified Square.par and native source files.
steps.note: Keep the archive with your modified Square.par. The ZIP and member hashes are retained with this case.

steps.title: What this changed case establishes
instructions: The mesh matches Basic exactly; changed maximum speed is descriptive context for the changed thickness input.
The hmax/hmin values are source-confirmed. The opaque saved MATLAB model was not decoded, and this experiment is not a repeat-equality or accuracy test.
steps.why: Keep the scientific input definitions and numerical qualifications with the result.
steps.expected: The Basic mesh matches; the changed speed is descriptive context, not accuracy validation.
